title: Errands
goal: Get things done around town — cash from the ATM, medicine from the pharmacy, a new SIM, a phone repair, the tailor, the barber, the laundry and the courier — and say "I got it fixed" and "I'm getting my hair cut" with causative verbs.
intro:
A normal Saturday in Hyderabad or Karachi is a chain of small jobs: the ATM, the **ميڊيڪل اسٽور**, the mobile shop in Saddar, the tailor who promised your Eid clothes 'tomorrow' last week, the barber, the dhobi and the TCS counter. This unit gives you the words for all of them and the one piece of grammar that errands run on: the **causative** — not 'I cut my hair' but **وار ڪٽايم** 'I *got* my hair cut', not 'I fixed it' but **ٺهرايو** 'I *got* it fixed'.

You'll also learn to pin down *when* something will be ready: ٻن ڏينهن **۾** 'in two days', شام **تائين** 'by the evening', عيد **کان اڳ** 'before Eid'.

grammar.title: Getting something done: causative verbs
grammar.body:
English says 'I **had** my hair cut', 'I **got** my phone fixed'. Sindhi builds this into the verb itself, with a **causative** ending:

• **-āiṇu** added to the stem: ڪٽڻ 'cut' → **ڪٽائڻ** kaṭāiṇu 'get cut' · ڪرڻ 'do' → **ڪرائڻ** karāiṇu 'get done'
• **-rāiṇu** on some verbs, especially ones whose plain form already means 'make/do': ٺاهڻ 'make, fix' → **ٺهرائڻ** ṭhahrāiṇu 'get made / fixed'

The new verb is a completely ordinary verb ending in -āiṇu, so it conjugates like هلائڻ or ڳالهائڻ:

مان ڪٽايان ٿو kaṭāyāṃ tho — I get (it) cut
مان ڪٽائيندس kaṭāīndus — I'll get (it) cut
مون کي ڪٽائڻو آهي kaṭāiṇo — I need to get (it) cut
مون ڪٽايو / ڪٽائي / ڪٽايا kaṭāyo / kaṭāī / kaṭāyā — I got (it) cut

**The past agrees with the thing**, because a causative is transitive (Unit 16): مون **سوٽ** ٺهرايو (m), مون **قميص** ٺهرائي (f), مون **وار** ڪٽايا (m pl). The doer is in the oblique with no marker: مون، هن، اسان، تو.

**The person who does the job** takes **کان** 'from': **حجام کان** وار ڪٽايا 'I had my hair cut by the barber', **درزيءَ کان** قميص ٺهرائي. You can also say where: حجام **وٽ** 'at the barber's'.

**Noun + ڪرائڻ** is the everyday workhorse: مرمت ڪرائڻ 'get repaired', استري ڪرائڻ 'get ironed', لوڊ ڪرائڻ 'get a top-up', جمع ڪرائڻ 'pay in'. When there is a separate object, the verb agrees with *it*, not with the noun in front: مون **ڪپڙا** استري **ڪرايا** (ڪپڙا m pl), even though استري is feminine.

**The trap**: using the plain verb. مون وار ڪٽيا means you cut your own hair (or someone else's!). If someone else did it, it must be the causative.

grammar.title: It broke · I fixed it · I got it fixed
grammar.body:
Many Sindhi verbs come in families of two or three, and choosing the right member is half of describing any errand:

**ٺهڻ** ṭhahaṇu — to *get* made / fixed (intransitive: the thing is the subject)
**ٺاهڻ** ṭhāhaṇu — to make / fix (transitive: someone does it)
**ٺهرائڻ** ṭhahrāiṇu — to get it made / fixed (causative: you have someone do it)

فون **ٺهي ويو** — the phone's been fixed (no doer mentioned)
دڪاندار فون **ٺاهيو** — the shopkeeper fixed the phone
مون فون **ٺهرايو** — I got the phone fixed

The same pattern with **ٿيڻ / ڪرڻ / ڪرائڻ**: مرمت **ٿي** 'the repair got done', هن مرمت **ڪئي** 'he did the repair', مون مرمت **ڪرائي** 'I had it repaired'. And with **ٽٽڻ** 'to break (by itself)' vs **ڀڃڻ** 'to break (something)': اسڪرين ٽٽي پئي 'the screen broke' — the polite, blame-free way to report damage.

The intransitive member agrees with the **thing** as subject and often takes **وڃڻ** or **پوڻ** to show completion: ٺهي ويو / ٺهي وئي 'got done', ٽٽي پيو / ٽٽي پئي 'broke'. The transitive and causative members follow the ergative past: oblique doer + verb agreeing with the object.

A quick test: *who did it?* Nobody mentioned → ٺهڻ / ٿيڻ. The speaker or someone else with their own hands → ٺاهڻ / ڪرڻ. The speaker, but by paying someone → ٺهرائڻ / ڪرائڻ.

examples.en: I got my phone fixed in Karachi.

examples.en: The cup fell from the child's hand and broke.

grammar.title: Ready when? ۾، تائين، کان اڳ، کان پوءِ
grammar.body:
Every errand ends with the same question: **ڪڏهن تيار ٿيندو؟** 'when will it be ready?' The answer uses a time word plus one of four little words:

**۾** meṃ — *within*: ٻن ڏينهن ۾ 'in two days', هڪ ڪلاڪ ۾ 'in an hour'
**تائين** tāīṃ — *by / until*: شام تائين 'by this evening', جمعي تائين 'by Friday'
**کان اڳ** khāṃ aɠu — *before*: عيد کان اڳ 'before Eid'
**کان پوءِ** khāṃ poi — *after*: ٻن وڳي کان پوءِ 'after two o'clock'

The time word goes into the **oblique** in front of these: ٻه ڏينهن → **ٻن ڏينهن** ۾ (ɓin ɗīṃhan), ٽي ڪلاڪ → **ٽن ڪلاڪن** ۾ (ṭin kalākan), جمعو → **جمعي** تائين (jumʿe). An infinitive can stand in too: پهچڻ کان پوءِ 'after arriving', وڃڻ کان اڳ 'before going' (oblique -a in speech: pahuchaṇa, vañaṇa).

The 'ready' sentence itself is usually the future of ٿيڻ or of a compound with وڃڻ: تيار **ٿيندو** (m) / **ٿيندي** (f); ٺهي **ويندو** / **ويندي** — agreeing with the thing that will be ready.

Don't confuse **۾** and **تائين**: ٻن ڏينهن ۾ = done within two days; ٻن ڏينهن تائين = it lasts for / until two days (e.g. closed for two days).

examples.en: The shirt will be ready in two days.
The phone will be fixed by this evening.

culture:
**Errands are social.** Your barber, tailor and mobile-shop man in Sindh soon become 'your' barber, 'your' tailor — you call them **ادا** or **سائين**, they offer you tea, and a small discount or a faster job comes from being a regular, not from arguing. Barbers' shops are the neighbourhood news desk; expect to be asked where you're from and whether you're married.

**Tailors and Eid**: everyone has clothes stitched (**ٺهرائڻ**) for Eid, so from mid-Ramazan tailors stop taking orders. Book two or three weeks ahead, and take 'it'll be ready tomorrow' (**سڀاڻي تيار**) with a pinch of salt — go back the day before you need it. Women's clothes go to women tailors or are ordered through a **پارلر** or boutique.

**SIMs** in Pakistan need your **شناختي ڪارڊ** (or passport) and a thumbprint (biometric verification) at an official franchise of Jazz, Zong, Telenor or Ufone. Top-ups (**لوڊ**) can be bought at any small shop. **Pharmacies** sell most medicines over the counter, and the person behind the counter will happily advise you — but antibiotics should really come with a **نسخو**. ATMs run dry before Eid and at the start of the month, when salaries land, so withdraw early. For parcels people use **TCS** or **Leopards**; give a landmark with the **پتو** ('near the Sindh Museum'), because street addresses alone often aren't enough.

tip.title: I need to… — the -ṇo form agrees
tip.body:
- **مون کي** + infinitive in **-ṇo** + آهي = I need to / I've got to (Unit 15).
- With an object, the -ṇo form agrees with it: پئسا **ڪڍڻا** (m pl), رسيد **وٺڻي** (f), کاتو **کولڻو** (m).
- No object → -ṇo: مون کي بئنڪ **وڃڻو** آهي.

tip.title: Getting it done: -āiṇu
tip.body:
- **ڪٽڻ** cut → **ڪٽائڻ** get cut; **ڪرڻ** do → **ڪرائڻ** get done.
- They conjugate like هلائڻ: ڪٽايان ٿو، ڪٽائيندس، ڪٽائڻو آهي.
- The person who does the job takes **کان**: حجام **کان** وار ڪٽايا.
- Plain ڪٽڻ = you cut it yourself.

sentences.en: My sister's going to the parlour before the wedding.

sentences.native: پارلر ۾ وار ڪٽائڻ ڏاڍو مهانگو آهي.
sentences.roman: pārlara meṃ vāra kaṭāiṇu ɗāḍho mahāngo āhe.
sentences.en: Getting your hair cut at a parlour is really expensive.

tip.title: I got it made — the past agrees with the thing
tip.body:
- A causative is transitive, so its past works like مون ڏٺو: the doer is oblique (مون، هن، تو) and the verb agrees with the **thing**.
- مون **سوٽ** ٺهرايو · مون **قميص** ٺهرائي · مون **ڪپڙا** ٺهرايا · مون **قميصون** ٺهرايون.
- استري ڪرائڻ: agree with the clothes, not with استري: **ڪپڙا** استري **ڪرايا**.
tip.pattern: مون + thing + ٺهرايو / ٺهرائي / ٺهرايا / ٺهرايون

sentences.native: عيد لاءِ نوان ڪپڙا ٺهرائڻا آهن.
sentences.roman: ʿīda lāi navāṃ kapiṛā ṭhahrāiṇā āhin.
sentences.en: I need to get new clothes made for Eid.

sentences.native: مون درزيءَ کان ٻه قميصون ٺهرايون.
sentences.roman: moṃ darzīa khāṃ ɓa qamīsūṃ ṭhahrāyūṃ.
sentences.en: I had two shirts made at the tailor's.

sentences.native: تو هيءَ قميص ڪٿان ٺهرائي؟
sentences.roman: to hīa qamīsa kithāṃ ṭhahrāī?
sentences.en: Where did you get this shirt made? (informal)

sentences.native: درزيءَ منهنجي ماپ ورتي.
sentences.roman: darzīa munhinjī māpa vartī.
sentences.en: The tailor took my measurements.

sentences.native: ادا، ماپ صحيح وٺجو!
sentences.roman: adā, māpa sahī vaṭhijo!
sentences.en: Please take the measurements properly!

sentences.native: مان ڪپڙا ڌوٻيءَ کي ڏيان ٿو.
sentences.roman: māṃ kapiṛā dhobīa khe ɗiyāṃ tho.
sentences.en: I give my clothes to the dhobi. (man)

sentences.native: مون ڪپڙا استري ڪرايا.
sentences.roman: moṃ kapiṛā istrī karāyā.
sentences.en: I got my clothes ironed.

sentences.native: هيءَ شلوار ٿوري ڊگهي آهي، ننڍي ڪرائڻي پوندي.
sentences.roman: hīa shalvāra thorī ḍighī āhe, nanḍhī karāiṇī pavandī.
sentences.en: These shalwar are a bit long — I'll have to get them shortened.

sentences.native: امان منهنجي اجرڪ ڌوٻيءَ کان استري ڪرائي.
sentences.roman: amāṃ munhinjī ajraka dhobīa khāṃ istrī karāī.
sentences.en: Mum had my ajrak ironed at the dhobi's.

lessons.title: A new SIM and a broken phone

tip.title: It broke · I fixed it · I got it fixed
tip.body:
- **ٺهڻ** get fixed (the thing is the subject): فون **ٺهي ويو**.
- **ٺاهڻ** fix: دڪاندار فون **ٺاهيو**.
- **ٺهرائڻ** get fixed: مون فون **ٺهرايو**.
- Same with **ٿيڻ / ڪرڻ / ڪرائڻ**, and **ٽٽڻ** 'break (by itself)': اسڪرين **ٽٽي پئي**.

new: منهنجي فون جي اسڪرين ٽٽي پئي آهي.

sentences.native: شڪر آهي، منهنجو فون ٺهي ويو.
sentences.roman: shukur āhe, munhinjo fon ṭhahī vayo.
sentences.en: Thank God, my phone is fixed.

sentences.native: دڪاندار فون اڌ ڪلاڪ ۾ ٺاهي ڏنو.
sentences.roman: dukāndāra fon adhu kalāka meṃ ṭhāhī ɗino.
sentences.en: The shopkeeper fixed the phone for me in half an hour.

sentences.native: مون فون صدر ۾ ٺهرايو.
sentences.roman: moṃ fon sadara meṃ ṭhahrāyo.
sentences.en: I got my phone fixed in Saddar.

sentences.native: منهنجو فون هٿ مان ڪري ٽٽي پيو.
sentences.roman: munhinjo fon hatha māṃ kirī ṭuṭī peyo.
sentences.en: My phone fell out of my hand and broke.

sentences.native: اسڪرين مٽائڻي پوندي.
sentences.roman: iskrīna maṭāiṇī pavandī.
sentences.en: The screen will have to be replaced.

sentences.native: مرمت ۾ ڪيترا پئسا لڳندا؟
sentences.roman: maramata meṃ ketirā paisā laɠandā?
sentences.en: How much will the repair cost?

sentences.native: هن جي سم بند ٿي وئي آهي.
sentences.roman: hun jī sima bandu thī vaī āhe.
sentences.en: His SIM has been blocked.

sentences.native: جڏهن فون چوري ٿيو ته مون سم بند ڪرائي.
sentences.roman: jaɗahiṃ fon chorī thiyo ta moṃ sima bandu karāī.
sentences.en: When my phone was stolen I had the SIM blocked.

sentences.native: نئين سم لاءِ شناختي ڪارڊ ضروري آهي.
sentences.roman: naīṃ sima lāi shanākhtī kārḍu zarūrī āhe.
sentences.en: You need your ID card for a new SIM.

sentences.native: ڪالهه لوڊ ڪرايو هو، سڄو ختم ٿي ويو!
sentences.roman: kālha loḍu karāyo ho, saʄo xatmu thī vayo!
sentences.en: I topped up only yesterday and it's all gone!

lessons.title: At the pharmacy

tip.title: Pills, syrups and "without"
tip.body:
- **گوري** (f) tablet: هڪ گوري، ٻه **گوريون**.
- **شربت** (m) syrup: مٺو شربت، کنگهه جو شربت.
- **کان سواءِ** = without, after the oblique: نسخي کان سواءِ.
- Doses: ڏينهن ۾ ٻه ڀيرا 'twice a day', ماني کان پوءِ 'after food'.

new: هي دوا نسخي کان سواءِ ملندي؟

sentences.native: ڏينهن ۾ ٻه گوريون کائو.
sentences.roman: ɗīṃha meṃ ɓa goryūṃ khāo.
sentences.en: Take two tablets a day.

sentences.native: هيءَ گوري ماني کان پوءِ کائجو.
sentences.roman: hīa gorī mānī khāṃ poi khāijo.
sentences.en: Take this tablet after food.

sentences.native: نسخي کان سواءِ اها دوا نه ملندي.
sentences.roman: nusxe khāṃ savāi uhā davā na milandī.
sentences.en: You can't get that medicine without a prescription.

sentences.native: ميڊيڪل اسٽور رات جو به کليل آهي؟
sentences.roman: meḍīkal isṭoru rāti jo bi khulyalu āhe?
sentences.en: Is the pharmacy open at night too?

sentences.native: ٻار لاءِ مٺو شربت ڏيو.
sentences.roman: ɓāra lāi miṭho sharbatu ɗiyo.
sentences.en: Can I have a sweet syrup for the child?

sentences.native: منهنجي ڊاڪٽر جو نسخو گم ٿي ويو.
sentences.roman: munhinje ḍākṭara jo nusxo gumu thī vayo.
sentences.en: I've lost my doctor's prescription.

sentences.native: مٿي جي سور لاءِ ڪا گوري ڏيو.
sentences.roman: mathe je sūra lāi kā gorī ɗiyo.
sentences.en: Can I have something for a headache?

sentences.native: هي شربت ڏينهن ۾ ٽي ڀيرا پيئو.
sentences.roman: hī sharbatu ɗīṃha meṃ ṭe bherā pīo.
sentences.en: Take this syrup three times a day.

sentences.native: ميڊيڪل اسٽور تان منهنجيون گوريون وٺي اچ.
sentences.roman: meḍīkal isṭora tāṃ munhinjūṃ goryūṃ vaṭhī achu.
sentences.en: Pick up my tablets from the pharmacy, would you? (informal)

lessons.title: Couriers, and "when will it be ready?"

tip.title: Within, by, before, after
tip.body:
- **۾** within: ٻن ڏينهن **۾**.
- **تائين** by / until: شام **تائين**.
- **کان اڳ** before, **کان پوءِ** after: عيد **کان اڳ**.
- The time word goes oblique: ٻه ڏينهن → **ٻن** ڏينهن ۾، جمعو → **جمعي** تائين.
tip.pattern: time (oblique) + ۾ / تائين / کان اڳ / کان پوءِ

new: هي سوٽ عيد تائين ٺهي ويندو؟

sentences.native: پارسل ٽن ڏينهن ۾ پهچي ويندو.
sentences.roman: pārsalu ṭin ɗīṃhan meṃ pahuchī vendo.
sentences.en: The parcel will get there in three days.

sentences.native: سوٽ سڀاڻي شام تائين تيار ٿي ويندو.
sentences.roman: sūṭu subhāṇe shāma tāīṃ tayāru thī vendo.
sentences.en: The suit will be ready by tomorrow evening.

sentences.native: مون کي فون جمعي کان اڳ گهرجي.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe fon jumʿe khāṃ aɠu ghurje.
sentences.en: I need the phone before Friday.

sentences.native: ڪوريئر وارو ٻن وڳي کان پوءِ ايندو.
sentences.roman: koriyara vāro ɓin vaɠe khāṃ poi endo.
sentences.en: The courier guy will come after two.

sentences.native: اهو ڪم هڪ ڪلاڪ ۾ ٿي ويندو.
sentences.roman: uho kamu hika kalāka meṃ thī vendo.
sentences.en: That'll be done within an hour.

sentences.native: ڪپڙا عيد کان اڳ ٺهي ويندا؟
sentences.roman: kapiṛā ʿīda khāṃ aɠu ṭhahī vendā?
sentences.en: Will the clothes be ready before Eid?

sentences.native: پنهنجو پتو لکي ڏيو.
sentences.roman: panhinjo pato likhī ɗiyo.
sentences.en: Write your address down for me, please.

sentences.native: مون ڪوريئر سان پارسل موڪليو هو، اڃا نه پهتو.
sentences.roman: moṃ koriyara sāṃ pārsalu mokilyo ho, añā na pahuto.
sentences.en: I sent a parcel by courier and it still hasn't arrived.

sentences.native: پتو غلط هو، تنهن ڪري پارسل واپس آيو.
sentences.roman: pato ġalatu ho, tanhin kare pārsalu vāpas āyo.
sentences.en: The address was wrong, so the parcel came back.

sentences.native: پارسل پهچڻ کان پوءِ فون ڪجو.
sentences.roman: pārsalu pahuchaṇa khāṃ poi fon kajo.
sentences.en: Give me a call once the parcel arrives.
